what_its_for: Stiripentol is used to help control seizures in people with a rare type of epilepsy called Dravet syndrome. It is always used together with other seizure medicines (clobazam and valproate) and is approved for patients 2 years of age and older who have seizures that are not fully controlled with those medicines alone.
how_to_take: Take stiripentol by mouth with food, during a meal. Never take it on an empty stomach, as this can cause stomach upset and may affect how well the medicine works. It comes as capsules (which you swallow whole) or as a powder in sachets (which you mix into a small amount of water, orange juice, or fruit-flavored syrup and drink right away). Do not crush or chew the capsules. Always take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate the right dose based on your body weight (usually 50 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, split into 2 or 3 doses). Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first. The total daily dose is usually between 1,000 mg and 3,000 mg per day, depending on weight. Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still close to your usual dosing time. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Missing doses may increase your risk of seizures.
storage: Store stiripentol capsules and sachets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from moisture and heat. Keep it away from direct sunlight. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package. If you mix the powder with liquid, drink it right away and do not store the mixed liquid.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol or taking products that contain alcohol while on stiripentol — this can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can cause drowsiness and slow your thinking. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, because stiripentol can interact with many medications including other seizure medicines, blood thinners, and cholesterol medicines. Avoid stopping this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this may cause more seizures.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a sudden increase in seizures or new types of seizures; thoughts of self-harm or suicide or new mood changes; severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling of the skin; signs of low blood cell counts such as unusual bruising, bleeding, fever, or repeated infections; severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; yellowing of the skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); extreme drowsiness, confusion, or difficulty waking up; or any allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Stiripentol does not work instantly. It may take several weeks before you notice a reduction in your seizures. Your doctor will monitor how well it is working and may adjust your dose during this time. Even if you feel well, keep taking your medicine every day. Do not stop taking it on your own — stopping suddenly can make seizures worse.
special_populations: Children: Stiripentol is approved for children aged 2 years and older. The dose is based on weight, so children may receive different amounts than adults. Older adults: Use with extra caution in elderly patients, as they may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and drowsiness. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may harm an unborn baby, and it is not known if it passes into breast milk. Kidney or liver problems: Let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver disease, as the dose may need to be adjusted or the medicine may not be right for you.
